h: Fenwick's committee backs a Gasworks streetcar
b: A council transport committee led by Councilwoman Odalys Fenwick voted 4-1 to fund a streetcar line linking the old Gasworks district to the ferry terminal. The 3.2-mile route would open in 2029 and cost $210 million, mostly from federal grants.

h: Dr. Ravindra Kessling named head of the Coldwater observatory
b: The university named astrophysicist Ravindra Kessling director of its Coldwater observatory, succeeding a founder who retired after thirty-one years. Kessling has led a survey of faint galaxies and plans to open the dome to school groups on weekends.

h: Brightwater Dairy recalls soft cheese
b: Brightwater Dairy recalled 12,000 wheels of soft cheese after a routine test found listeria. No illnesses were reported. Shoppers were told to throw the product away or return it to the store for a refund.

h: Marlowe Textiles workers end eleven-day strike
b: About 400 employees at the Marlowe Textiles mill returned to work on Monday after accepting a three-year agreement with a 9 percent raise. The walkout began over mandatory overtime and a plan to freeze pensions.

h: Quillfeather Games delays Nightbloom
b: Quillfeather Games said its fantasy role-playing title Nightbloom will launch in March instead of December, saying the extra months would be used to fix performance problems on older consoles.

h: Fog cancels Tern Island ferry
b: Ferries to Tern Island did not run on Thursday because dense fog cut visibility to under 200 feet. Residents of the offshore community were stranded on the mainland overnight, and the mail boat was held at its pier.

h: Halvard Pharmaceuticals ordered to pay $62 million
b: A federal judge ordered Halvard Pharmaceuticals to pay $62 million for misleading doctors about how addictive its painkiller was. The company said it would appeal the ruling and noted that it stopped selling the drug in 2022.

h: Silvermine schools adopt a four-day week
b: The Silvermine school board voted 4-1 to hold classes Monday through Thursday beginning next autumn, lengthening each day by forty minutes. The district said the change would save $1.1 million and help it keep teachers.

h: Ostrander Rail Bridge cleared for freight
b: The Ostrander Rail Bridge reopened to freight trains after a three-week inspection found the steel piers sound. Two grain shippers had rerouted cars through a yard 90 miles away during the closure.

h: Mayor Vance proposes ban on gas leaf blowers
b: Mayor Teodora Vance asked the council to prohibit gasoline-powered leaf blowers within city limits by next fall, citing noise and exhaust. Landscaping firms said battery models cost twice as much and run half as long.

h: Nimbus Cloud outage lasts six hours
b: Nimbus Cloud customers lost access to storage and databases for six hours on Tuesday after an expired security certificate in a core service. The company apologized and promised credits to affected accounts.

h: Harborview Hospital nurses ratify contract
b: Nurses at Harborview Hospital ratified a three-year contract by 82 percent, winning raises of 11 percent and limits on mandatory shifts. The union had threatened a walkout on December 1.

h: Lead found in Dunmore school fountains
b: Testing found lead above the federal action level in drinking fountains at six Dunmore schools. The fountains were shut and bottled water was delivered while the district replaced pipes and fixtures.

h: Avalanche kills two skiers on Cobalt Peak
b: Two backcountry skiers died when an avalanche swept them down the north face of Cobalt Peak on Saturday. Rescuers recovered the bodies the next morning. Avalanche forecasters had rated the danger as considerable.

h: Pelham growers lose half the harvest to frost
b: Grape growers around Pelham said an early hard frost destroyed roughly half of this year's crop. Several vineyards will make no reserve wine, and the county asked for disaster aid.

h: Arc Motors recalls 48,000 electric SUVs
b: Arc Motors is recalling 48,000 battery-powered utility vehicles because a software error can delay braking when the car is in regenerative mode. Dealers will install an update free of charge.

h: Prosecutors drop charges against Marcus Teague
b: Prosecutors dropped all charges against Marcus Teague, a bus mechanic accused of stealing parts, after the main witness recanted. Teague said he wants his job back and an apology.

h: Fire destroys the old Saltmarsh lighthouse cottage
b: A fire early Sunday destroyed the keeper's cottage beside the Saltmarsh lighthouse, a building from 1871. The tower itself was undamaged. Investigators said an old chimney is the likely cause.

h: Eastbrook food bank sees demand up 30 percent
b: The Greater Eastbrook Food Bank said it served 30 percent more households than a year ago and that shelves are nearly empty before the holidays. Volunteers asked for canned protein and baby formula.

h: Senator Brandvold unveils the Open Meadows Act
b: Senator Ilse Brandvold introduced the Open Meadows Act, which would pay ranchers to leave grassland unplowed and open it to hikers and hunters. The bill has eleven co-sponsors from both parties.

h: Fenwick Orchards sells forty acres for housing
b: Fenwick Orchards agreed to sell forty acres of apple trees to a builder planning 220 homes. The family said rising taxes made farming unaffordable.

h: Brightwater Reservoir falls to a record low
b: The Brightwater Reservoir dropped to its lowest level on record after a dry autumn, and the water district asked customers to cut outdoor use.

h: Marlowe Street to get speed cameras
b: The city will install speed cameras on Marlowe Street near two schools, with warnings for the first thirty days.

h: Silvermine hikers rescued after night on the ridge
b: Three hikers were rescued from the Silvermine ridge after becoming lost in fog. All were treated for exposure.

h: Harborview Mall to lose its anchor store
b: The department store anchoring Harborview Mall will close in January, leaving a third of the space empty.

h: Brandvold Foundation gives $5 million to the county library
b: The Brandvold Foundation gave $5 million to rebuild the main branch of the county library, which will gain a children's wing.
